name: Phosphorus Oxychloride
description: Phosphorus Oxychloride (CAS 10025-87-3), also known as phosphoryl chloride, is a critical process chemical in solar photovoltaic cell manufacturing. It serves as the primary phosphorus dopant source in the diffusion doping process for crystalline silicon solar cells, creating the n-type emitter layer essential for the p-n junction. The compound is also widely used in organic synthesis as a chlorinating and dehydrating agent for producing phosphate esters, pharmaceutical intermediates, and flame retardants. In semiconductor applications, ultra-high purity grades ensure consistent doping profiles and optimal cell efficiency. Phosphorus Oxychloride is a colorless to pale yellow fuming liquid that reacts vigorously with water and must be handled under strict moisture-free conditions.
physicalProperties: Appearance: colorless to pale yellow fuming liquid; Molecular Weight: 153.33 g/mol; Boiling Point: 105.8 °C; Melting Point: 1.25 °C; Density: 1.645 g/cm³; Vapor Pressure: 40 mmHg at 27.3°C; Refractive Index: 1.4609
